name: OpenRouter host selection and sampling controls
highlights: Choose the serving host within OpenRouter and set sampling temperature explicitly. Connection tests and AI tools share these settings; diagnostics record the sent route and temperature.

AI requests no longer automatically repeat when the endpoint exhausts its output budget before answering. Errors explain reported reasoning usage and provider selection; active auto-orient diagnostics include elapsed timings.
Auto-orient shows elapsed waits and JSON repair attempts, supports cancellation, and exports timing diagnostics without sharing API keys or CAD images.
AI batches preserve provider thinking defaults. Reasoning changes are explicit settings, and optional price lookups no longer delay auto-orient or component identification.

AI output-token and request-time limits are user-configurable, with no application-imposed limit by default. OpenRouter connection tests explain provider, credit, authentication and browser-network failures.
Model loading and cached reopening are more responsive, with stronger source-identity checks and safeguards against incomplete assembly imports.
Photoreal rendering reuses shader preparation more effectively, recovers from interrupted GPU warm-up, and improves material scaling and smooth-glass behavior.
AI design review links suggested checks to local measurements and component evidence, distinguishes facts from suggestions, and invalidates outdated results when the model changes.
AI connection tests can be cancelled, reject malformed replies and stop when settings change; large-assembly review preparation stays interactive while counting candidate pairs.
Engineering readouts preserve calculation precision, distinguish known mass from incomplete totals, and keep saved review evidence tied to the correct model session.
